newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firm at close on Cetes, U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firm at close on Cetes, U.S. long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso held on to midsession gains to close firm across the board on Wednesday due to gains in domestic interest rates while U.S. long bond yields were down, traders said.
"The peso met with strong resistance at 7.89 per dollar, despite the outcome of last night's Cetes auction and low U.S. long bond yields," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.8930/7.8960 and 7.8900/7.8930 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 18.91 percent at Tuesday night's auction, an increase of 54 basis points since last week, but less than the 76-basis point rise forecast.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 14/32 to yield 6.89 percent in late trade, following what traders said were mild U.S. producer price data.

Dealers said the peso failed to gain more ground due to caution ahead of the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rate policy, even though recent data suggest the U.S. economy is not overheating.
"I believe tomorrow's (retail sales) data will be favorable, but even so dealers are taking care with next Tuesday's (FOMC) meeting coming up," a trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.6 centavos firmer at 7.8860/7.8890 per dollar.
Dealers expected the 48-hour peso to lose some ground to the dollar on Thursday due to swaps as these contracts do not come due until after the weekend.
